newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VETERAN ZUBIZARRETA FACES UP TO THE RONALDO PHENOMENON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VETERAN ZUBIZARRETA FACES UP TO THE RONALDO PHENOMENON.

text.p: After spending more than half of his life in the star-studded Spanish league, Valencia's international goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta could have been forgiven for thinking he'd seen it all.

But Saturday's game at leaders Barcelona puts the veteran "Zubi" up against his former club and an opponent who promises to be tougher than Maradona, Butragueno, Hugo Sanchez and everyone else the 80s and 90s could offer.
In Barcelona, as the Spanish papers say, 'goal' is pronounced 'Ronaldo.'
The 20-year old Brazilian has exhausted the superlatives of even the most garrulous Spanish commentators with a string of amazing performances in which he has averaged a goal a game.
While Ronaldo has been in outstanding form, there will be no confrontation with his compatriot Romario, who has walked out on Valencia, gone home and will miss the game against his former club.
Romario's future was still in the balance on Friday after Brazilians Flamengo broke off negotiations to take the striker back on loan.
Gabriel Moya has blossomed in Romario's absence, leading Valencia to three wins in a row.
But Valencia had Zubizarreta to thank for the second of those victories, a superb 3-1 win over Atletico Madrid.
The game was just six minutes old when Juan Eduardo Esnaider forced an incredible reflex save from the keeper, whom he embraced in disbelief afterwards.
Zubizarreta, who won four Spanish titles and a European Cup at Barcelona before moving to Valencia two seasons ago, has consistently proved wrong those who have tried to write him off.
And after making his first division debut aged just 17, Zubi celebrated his 35th birthday with another victory -- 2-1 over Sporting Gijon -- on Wednesday.
"Sometimes I watch videos of games I played some years ago, and it scares me," said Zubizarreta. "But I continue having a great time."

One man that won't be spoiling Zubizarreta's great time this weekend is Juan Pizzi. Bobby Robson has dropped the international striker after Pizzi was visibly annoyed by being substituted after only playing 24 minutes of Wednesday's match at Sevilla.
